task: T1: add the artifact push helper to scripts/ralph-log.sh and wire it into the four writers that already produce artifacts. Define one helper taking the task label, the attempt number, a kind, and the path of the file just written; it POSTs that file's bytes to `{base}/runs/{run_key}/attempts/{task}/{attempt}/artifacts/{kind}`, where `{task}` is the SHORT label produced by the existing `log_task` helper — `T1`, not the task's prose, which is what `log_task` already reduces `T1: make a.` to for the artifact's own filename. Reuse that helper rather than re-deriving the slug, so an artifact's URL and its filename always name the same task; the full task text already travels in the status record and has no business in a URL. using the SAME configuration the status channel uses — `HARNESS_REPORT_URL` for the base, `HARNESS_REPORT_TOKEN` as a bearer header — and reusing the transport helper `scripts/ralph-status.sh` already provides rather than writing a second one. Two posting paths would drift, and the second one is always the one that leaks the token or blocks. Derive the run key the same way, from the identity the loop already has; do not mint a second one. Call it from `log_prompt`, `log_gate`, `log_failure`, `log_patch` and `log_meta`, each with its own kind — `prompt`, `gate`, `diff`, `patch`, `meta`. `patch` and `diff` are separate kinds because they are separate artifacts written on opposite outcomes: `log_patch` runs when an attempt PASSES and holds the change that was kept, `log_failure` runs when one FAILS and holds the verify output plus the work about to be discarded. Most tasks pass, so omitting `patch` would mean a reader can see the files a task changed only when the task failed. Post each immediately after each writes its file, and only when that write succeeded: an artifact that was never written must not be announced as one that was. When no URL is configured the loop must do nothing at all and print nothing, which is the required behaviour and not a degraded mode. Failure of a push must be silent and total, bounded by a short timeout, and must never fail, stall or alter the run. The token must never appear in any output. Do not push the executor transcript in this task; T3 owns it. Do not add polling, controls or retention logic.
